subject: biology
title: Why Siblings Differ
welcome_lead: Explore how brothers and sisters can look so different from the same family.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on variation between siblings and inheritance.
final_note: You now know why family members share features but are never identical.

concepts.def: Sperm and egg containing half DNA.
Sperm meets egg to form a new cell.
Two people from one fertilised egg.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each sperm and egg carries a unique combination of the parents' genes. Each fertilisation produces a new mix, so siblings receive different combinations.
Identical twins come from one fertilised egg that splits, so they share the same DNA. Non-identical twins come from two eggs and differ like normal siblings.
Even identical twins can look slightly different because of environment — diet, exercise and lifestyle change features like weight or skin tone.
